source_title: Total Number and Ratio of GABAergic Neuron Types in the Mouse Lateral and Basal Amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Directly quantifies all major BLA GABAergic interneuron types: axo-axonic cells (5.5-6%), PV basket cells (17-20%), CCK basket cells (7-9%), SST dendrite-targeting cells (10-16%), NPY neurogliaform cells (14-15%), VIP/calretinin interneuron-selective interneurons (29-38%), and SST/nNOS GABAergic projection neurons (5.5-8%). Covers bla_pv_basket_cell, bla_axo_axonic_cell, bla_sst_interneuron, bla_cck_basket_cell, bla_vip_calretinin_interneuron, bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell, bla_gabaergic_projection_neuron.
summary: Vereczki et al. 2021 (preprint) provide the first unbiased stereological estimate of GABAergic neuron ratios in the mouse lateral (LA) and basal (BA) amygdala. GABAergic neurons constitute 16% of neurons in LA and 22% in BA (higher than hippocampus 20%, but comparable to neocortex). The seven cardinal inhibitory cell types are: axo-axonic cells (5.5-6%), PV+ basket cells (17-20%), CCK+ basket cells (7-9%), SST+ dendrite-targeting cells (10-16%), NPY+ neurogliaform cells (14-15%), VIP/calretinin interneuron-selective interneurons (29-38%), and SST+/nNOS+ GABAergic projection neurons (5.5-8%). No sex or hemisphere differences were found. These types together account for the vast majority of GABAergic cells in the BLA.
quotes: axo-axonic cells (5.5%-6%), basket cells expressing parvalbumin (17%-20%) or cholecystokinin (7%-9%), dendrite-targeting inhibitory cells expressing somatostatin (10%-16%), NPY-containing neurogliaform cells (14%-15%), VIP and/or calretinin-expressing interneuron-selective interneurons (29%-38%), and GABAergic projection neurons expressing somatostatin and neuronal nitric oxide synthase (5.5%-8%)

summary: Discussion section of Vereczki et al. 2021: SST+ inhibitory cells in the BLA target predominantly the dendritic shaft and to a lesser extent the spines of principal cells, analogous to hippocampus and neocortex. SST+/nNOS+ cells are identified as GABAergic projection neurons; the ratio of SST+ interneurons in the amygdala (10-16%) is higher than hippocampus (4-5%) and similar to neocortex (17-20%). NPY is frequently expressed in neurogliaform cells, with ~45% of NPY+ GABAergic cells being neurogliaform cells (lacking PV, SST, and CB). VIP/calretinin interneuron-selective interneurons constitute 29-38% of GABAergic cells—the largest subpopulation—suggesting massive regulatory potential over other GABAergic cells in amygdala functions including affective memory formation.
quotes: SST+ inhibitory cells target predominantly the dendritic shaft and to a lesser extent, the spines of principal cells
NPY has been shown to be expressed often in neurogliaform cells

summary: Detailed analysis of NPY+ inhibitory cells in the LA and BA. Among NPY+ GABAergic neurons visualized with Npy-Cre;Dlx5/6-Flp strategy: approximately 25% co-express PV, approximately 27% co-express SST, and approximately 45% lack PV, SST, and CB immunoreactivity—this last subgroup corresponds to neurogliaform cells. The ratio of NPY+ inhibitory cells differed significantly between LA and BA. Pure neurogliaform cells represent approximately 45% of NPY+ GABAergic cells, confirming NPY as a marker for this cell type but noting extensive co-expression with PV and SST in other subpopulations.

summary: Introduction of Vereczki et al. 2021: The BLA is a nuclear extension of the cortex deep in the temporal lobe, consisting of the lateral (LA), basal (BA), and accessory basal nuclei. Principal cells use glutamate for fast neurotransmission; GABAergic neurons constitute ~15% in rat and ~25% in monkey. Cortical inhibitory neurons are heterogeneous; cardinal types include axo-axonic cells (with or without parvalbumin), basket cells, dendrite-targeting SST+ cells, and interneuron-selective cells. Prior studies had not separated distinct BLA nuclei, sexes, or hemispheres.
quotes: The BLA, which is a nuclear extension of the cortex deep in the temporal lobe, consists of the lateral (LA), basal (BA) and accessory basal nuclei
the principal neurons in these regions use glutamate as an excitatory neurotransmitter

summary: Hochgerner et al. 2023 used single-cell RNA sequencing on whole amygdala from 23 naive and fear-conditioned mice to generate a comprehensive cell taxonomy. summary: Hochgerner et al. 2023 describe two main branches of amygdala inhibitory cells based on Wfs1/Meis2/Ptk2b versus Maf/Zeb2 expression. Striatal MSN-like projecting neurons (CEA and IA) express Ptk2b, Zfhx3, Zfhx4, and Meis2. MGE-derived cortical-like interneurons (Sst, Pvalb, Vip, Sncg) express Nfib, Nfix, Tcf4, Satb1, Prox1 and form the Maf/Zeb2 branch. A third branch (GABA-22 to GABA-34) expresses Tshz2, Satb1, and Lhx6, consistent with MEA-projecting inhibitory cell types; this group is neuropeptide-rich (galanin/vasopressin, Nts, Sst). Intercalated cell types (GABA-5 to GABA-7) express Tacr3, Tshz2, Enpp2, Nts, and Cyp26a1 but are located in the CEA.
quotes: Local/interneuron markers Nfib, Nfix, Tcf4, Satb1 and Prox1 were expressed among canonical medial ganglionic eminences (MGE)-and caudal ganglionic eminences (CGE)-derived interneuron types (for example, Sst, Pvalb, Vip or Sncg)
This group was consistent with Lhx + MEA-projecting inhibitory cell types and was rich in neuropeptide expression

node_relevance_reason: Directly demonstrates SST+ GABAergic projection neurons in the BLA projecting to basal forebrain; about one-third co-express calbindin or NPY; about half co-express GAD. Directly relevant to bla_gabaergic_projection_neuron (SST/nNOS) and bla_sst_interneuron.
summary: McDonald et al. 2012: A subpopulation of SST+ non-pyramidal neurons (termed 'long-range non-pyramidal neurons', LRNP neurons) in the external capsule, BLA, and cortical/medial amygdalar nuclei project to the basal forebrain (BF). About one-third of these SST+ LRNP neurons co-express calbindin (CB) or NPY; about half co-express GAD. The great majority of amygdalar FG+ retrograde-labeled neurons did not express non-pyramidal markers, indicating the LRNP population is a distinct minority. This establishes GABAergic long-range projection neurons in the BLA with SST as a key marker, distinct from SST+ local interneurons.

summary: McDonald et al. 2012 results: Virtually all LRNP neurons in the corticobasolateral amygdala (CBL) expressed SOM. The CBL contains pyramidal-like projection neurons using glutamate and spine-sparse GABAergic interneurons. Four distinct GABAergic interneuron subpopulations are identified by calcium-binding proteins and peptides: (1) PV+/CB+ neurons, (2) SOM+/CB+ neurons, (3) large multipolar CCK+ neurons (often CB+), and (4) small bipolar/bitufted interneurons with extensive co-localization of calretinin (CR), CCK, and VIP. SST+/nNOS+ cells identified as projection neurons to basal forebrain. Co-expression of SOM and nNOS in projection neurons also noted.
quotes: four distinct subpopulations of GABAergic non-pyramidal neurons that can be distinguished on the basis of their content of calcium-binding proteins and peptides. These subpopulations are: (1) PV+/CB+ neurons, (2) SOM+/CB+ neurons, (3) large multipolar cholecystokinin+ neurons that are often CB+, and (4) small bipolar and bitufted interneurons that exhibit extensive colocalization of calretinin, cholecystokinin, and vasoactive intestinal peptide

summary: Pitkanen & Amaral 1994: Used immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization for GABA and GAD65/GAD67 in macaque monkey amygdala. GABA-immunoreactive neurons constitute ~20% of neuronal population in the lateral nucleus. Highest GABAergic cell densities in intercalated nuclei, amygdalohippocampal area, and posterior cortical nucleus. Lowest densities in central and medial nuclei—but despite low GABAergic neuron density, terminal density in the central nucleus was among the highest, indicating dense local GABAergic circuits from extrinsic inputs. Three morphological classes of GABA+ aspiny cells identified. ISH with GAD65/GAD67 probes labeled far more cells than immunohistochemistry in central, medial, and anterior cortical nuclei.
quotes: higher densities located in the intercalated nuclei, amygdalohippocampal area, and posterior cortical nucleus

The lowest densities of labeled cells were observed in the central and medial nuclei. Interestingly, despite the low number of GABA-immunoreactive neurons, the terminal density in the central nucleus was among the highest in the amygdala

summary: Full abstract of Pitkanen & Amaral 1994: The primate amygdala comprises at least 13 different nuclei. GABAergic neurons are throughout the amygdala (~20% in lateral nucleus), with highest densities in intercalated nuclei; three general classes of immunopositive aspiny cells are identified. The discrepancy between immunohistochemistry and ISH in the central nucleus (ISH labels far more cells) may relate to methodological sensitivity (colchicine, antibody specificity). Terminal density in the central nucleus is paradoxically high despite low cell body count, indicating dense incoming GABAergic input. These data provide baseline for understanding GABAergic dysfunction in amygdala-related disorders.

node_relevance_reason: Describes the paralaminar nucleus (PL) of the human amygdala: DCX+ PSA-NCAM+ immature neurons with delayed maturation; BCL2+ cells; CGE origin (SP8, PROX1, NR2F2/COUP-TFII); contrast with rodent intercalated nuclei. Directly relevant to paralaminar_immature_neuron.
summary: Sorrells et al. 2019: In the adult human amygdala, the paralaminar nucleus (PL) is located near the dorsal wall of the temporal lateral ventricle, next to the caudal ganglionic eminence (CGE). CGE expresses SP8, PROX1, and COUP-TFII (NR2F2)—transcription factors also present in PL cells. In rodents, dense clusters of GABAergic cells near the BLA (intercalated nuclei) are similar in location to the PL but do not express DCX and PSA-NCAM, and are not excitatory. Both intercalated nuclei and PL contain BCL2+ cells in non-human primates. PL cells in rodent intercalated nuclei are GABAergic and lineage-traced to the dorsal LGE, expressing SP8. The identity and embryonic development of human PL cells expressing DCX, PSA-NCAM, BCL2, SP8, PROX1, NR2F2 in an immature/delayed-maturation state is the focus of this study.
quotes: In the adult human amygdala the PL is located near the dorsal wall of the tLV, next to the caudal ganglionic eminence (CGE), a site of birth of GABAergic inhibitory interneurons during embryonic and fetal development that expresses the transcription factors SP8, PROX1, and COUP-TFII (Nr2f2)

section: AACs in the amygdaloid complex and extended amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterizes axo-axonic cells (AACs) across all amygdala nuclei using intersectional genetic strategy; demonstrates AACs in BLA, basomedial amygdala, cortical amygdala, and MeA but not CeA; density correlates with GLU PN abundance; morphology in amygdala distinct from neocortex. Directly relevant to bla_axo_axonic_cell and provides structural context for bla_glutamatergic_principal_neuron.
summary: Raudales et al. 2024 (eLife): Using an intersectional strategy (Nkx2.1Flp × Unc5bCreER; Ai65) for comprehensive AAC targeting in mouse brain, AACs were found in all amygdala nuclei containing glutamatergic projection neurons—BLA (LA/BA), basomedial amygdala (BMA), cortical amygdala (CoA), and medial amygdala (MeA)—but NOT in the central amygdala (CeA), which lacks glutamatergic PNs. In CeA, MeA, and BST (subpallium-derived, predominantly GABAergic), pAACs may innervate the minor glutamatergic PN population. The density of AACs correlates with GLU PN abundance: BLA, CoA, and BMA show much higher densities than MeA and BST. Within pallium-derived subdivisions (LA, BLA, BMA, PA), AAC densities are roughly similar. Morphologically, BLA AACs exhibit multipolar dendrites and multipolar axon terminal branches, distinct from neocortical AACs (which typically extend above or below the soma). AIS-targeting identity confirmed by AnkG co-staining (97.2%, n=36 cells). This paper establishes Nkx2.1 + Unc5b as markers for comprehensive genetic access to BLA axo-axonic cells.
quotes: we found AACs or pAACs in all the amygdala nuclei containing GLU PNs, that is except CeA
The density of AACs in amygdala appears to correlate with the known abundance of GLU PNs: densities in BLA, CoA, and BMA were much higher than those in MeA and BST

summary: Vicario et al. 2014: The mammalian central extended amygdala includes the central nucleus, intercalated amygdalar cells, lateral BSTL, and a sublenticular corridor. The intercalated amygdalar cells form an interface between infralimbic prefrontal cortex + lateral/BLA on one hand and the central amygdala on the other, and are involved in extinction of fear memories. The central amygdala is involved in acquisition, consolidation, and expression of fear conditioning. BSTL mediates contextual fear and long-lasting anxiety-like responses. The central extended amygdala projects via GABAergic descending projections to hypothalamic and brainstem targets.

summary: Vicario et al. 2014: The classic serial model of fear circuitry: lateral amygdala (sensory input) → central amygdala (fear expression via descending GABAergic projections to hypothalamus/brainstem) → BST (pallidal-like output). Updated view: lateral and central extended amygdalar nuclei operate in parallel through multiple circuitries involving distinct intercalated cell groups and distinct neuron types of the BLA, CEA, and BST to mediate different aspects of fear conditioning or extinction. The CEA operates both directly (descending projections) and indirectly (via BST) for fear expression.
quotes: rather than serially, it appears that the lateral and central extended amygdalar nuclei operate in parallel through multiple circuitries, which involve projections through distinct intercalated cell groups and distinct neuron types of the basolateral amygdala, central amygdala and BST, to mediate different aspects of fear conditioning or extinction

summary: Vicario et al. 2014: The central amygdala is a mosaic-like structure with cells from multiple embryonic domains. (1) LGEd-derived cells express Pax6 and locate in the capsular/lateral subdivisions (enkephalinergic neurons). (2) LGEv-derived cells express Islet1 and locate in lateral/medial subdivisions (CRF, dynorphin, calbindin neurons). (3) MGE-derived cells express Nkx2.1 and contain somatostatin, concentrating in the medial subdivision. These neuropeptidergic populations subserve different functions: ENK cells (emotional pain control), CRF cells (sustained/anxiety-like fear), SST cells (medial subdivision). Avian study used to infer mammalian homologs.
quotes: cells derived from the MGE express Nkx2.1 and contain somatostatin, and show a trend to concentrate in the medial subdivision of the nucleus
